newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end 2.32 pct weaker on Negara news.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end 2.32 pct weaker on Negara news.

text.p: The market plunged 2.32 percent as institutional investors dumped stocks following warnings by the central bank against currency speculators, dealers said.

The warnings included the possibility of higher Malaysian interest rates and raised fears of volatility in the ringgit. The ringgit has been under pressure from overseas selling in the wake of the Thai baht crisis.
At the close, the key Composite Index of large-capitalised stocks fell 24.53 points to 1,033.24. It fell to as low as 1.028.16 in afternoon trade.

"The concern is that if attacks continue on the ringgit, they will be forced to keep interest rates at higher levels. That could jeopardise infrastructure financing," said Song Seng Wun, regional economist at ABN Amro Hoare Govett.
Higher interest rates would also crimp corporate earnings, other analysts said.

The market had been weak in recent sessions as foreign investors trimmed their portfolios amid general bearishness over regional markets. Dealers said some of the stock-sales were linked to positions taken by hedge funds in preparation for an attack on the ringgit.
